sentences.text:
THIS PETITION IS COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
 THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC:6543  CRL.P No. 1222 of 2024  ORDER

This petition is filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C., by the petitioner seeking anticipatory bail in a case registered in Crime No.6/2024 of Chikkaballapura Town Police Station, for the offence punishable under Section 498A, 302 r/w 34 of IPC and Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

2. Heard the learned counsel for petitioner, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent/State and perused the material on record.
3.

In the complaint lodged by the father of the deceased, it is averred that his daughter by name Varalakshmi P.S. was given in marriage to the petitioner on 25.03.2019 at one Seetharama Kalyana Mantappa and two months after the marriage, the petitioner started subjecting her to cruelty in connection with dowry etc, on account of which she committed suicide by hanging herself, on 17.01.2024 in the Police quarters, Chikkaballapura.
NC: 2024:KHC:6543 4.
The aforementioned case is registered against the petitioner, his parents and other relatives.

5. The learned counsel for petitioner has enclosed a copy of the order passed by the Court of Principal Judge, Family Court at Chikkaballapura in M.C.No.14/2023 dated 13.06.2023, wherein the marriage between the petitioner and the deceased was dissolved by a decree of divorce.

entities.text: Court of Principal Judge, Family Court at Chikkaballapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 6. The marriage between the petitioner and the complainant's daughter - Varalakshmi P.S. took place on 25.03.2019.
It is not alleged in the complaint that at the time of marriage the petitioner has demanded any dowry.
As per the order passed in M.C.No.14/2023, the marriage has been dissolved by a decree of divorce on 13.06.2023.
The deceased committed suicide on 17.01.2024 in the police quarters, Chikkaballapura.
According to the prosecution even after divorce was granted, the deceased and the petitioner were living in the very same quarters.
It is alleged that the petitioner was mentally harassing the deceased.
As seen from the material placed on record, the relationship between the couple was not cordial.
Sri. Venkataramana.

2

entities.text: R. K vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The marriage was not consummated.
Several panchayats were held and the petitioner herein got issued a legal notice requesting the deceased to discharge her marital obligation.
Since there was no response from her, he filed a petition for divorce.
8. At this stage there is no sufficient material to show that soon before her death, the deceased was subjected to physical or mental cruelty by the petitioner.
The allegations have to be proved in due course in a full- fledged trial.
Petitioner is working as a Police constable.
He has undertaken to cooperate with the investigation and to furnish adequate surety to ensure his regular presence before the trial Court.

Hence, the following:
ORDER 1. Petition is allowed.

In the event of arrest of the petitioner/ accused in Crime No.6/2024 of Chikkaballapura Town Police Station, he shall be released subject to following conditions:
a) He shall appear before the Investigation Officer within a period of one week from the date of receipt of a copy of this order and shall execute a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) with two sureties for the likesum.
b) He shall furnish proof of his residential address and shall inform the Investigating Officer/Court, if there is any change in the address.
c) He shall make himself available for the purpose of investigation as and when required and shall co-operate with the investigation.
d) He shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses either directly or indirectly.
e) He shall be regular in attending the Court proceedings.
NC: 2024:KHC:6543 f) He shall not indulge himself in any criminal activity.

SD/-
JUDGE HB Sri. Venkataramana.
